skills.name: Daily-needs words; capital letters and spelling

note.text:
Basic daily needs are the things we need every day to live well: food, water, clothing, shelter (a home), soap, sleep and health care.
Useful words: rice, beans, plantains, bread, oil, salt, soap, toothbrush, toothpaste, bucket, blanket, mattress, sandals, uniform.
Spelling conventions:
• Use a capital letter for the names of people and places, for days and months, and for the word I: Ayuk, Bamenda, Monday, October.
• Start every sentence with a capital letter.
• Do not use a capital letter for ordinary words in the middle of a sentence: rice, soap, market.
• Learn words that are often misspelt: Wednesday, February, vegetables, necessary, toothpaste.
• Clothes are what we wear; cloths are pieces of cloth.
Check every word you write. A dictionary can help.

vars.wrong: on wensday, my mother bought sope and bred at the market in kumba.

worked_example.problem: Correct the capital letters and the spelling: “{wrong}”
steps: A sentence starts with a capital letter: On.
Days of the week take a capital letter, and this one is spelt Wednesday.
Kumba is the name of a town, so it takes a capital letter: Kumba.
Ordinary words stay small, but check their spelling: soap, bread, market.
worked_example.answer: On Wednesday, my mother bought soap and bread at the market in Kumba.

cards.idea: Basic daily needs are things we cannot live well without: food, water, clothing and shelter. Soap, sleep and health care are needs too.
example: Clothing: a shirt, a uniform, sandals.
Keeping clean: soap, a toothbrush, toothpaste.

cards.idea: Names of people and towns, days, months and the word I always start with a capital letter. So does every sentence.
example: Ayuk went to Bamenda on Saturday.
In October, I buy a new uniform.

cards.idea: Some everyday words are often misspelt. Learn them carefully.
example: clothes (what we wear) — cloths (pieces of cloth)

questions.prompt: Sort each word into its group.

Which word in this sentence needs a capital letter?
“{k == 'n' ? lowerAll(n) : n} bought {it} in {k == 't' ? lowerAll(t) : t} on {k == 'd' ? lowerAll(d) : d}.”

misconceptions.explain: “{it}” is an ordinary word, not a name: no capital letter.
“bought” is an ordinary word in the middle of the sentence: no capital letter.
“on” is a small ordinary word: no capital letter.

solution: “{answer}” is the name of {k == 'n' ? 'a person' : k == 't' ? 'a town' : 'a day'}, so it needs a capital letter: {k == 'n' ? n : k == 't' ? t : d}.

misconceptions.explain: Not quite. Say the word slowly and look at each letter again.
